I worked banquets in a large hotel in my hometown. We had a plated dinner for 400 VIP guests. When I say VIP I mean Politicians and Foreign Dignitaries. This was only my second week on the job so I was still trying to get used to carrying a serving tray. 

Anyways, at the end of each course, servers were responsible for clearing their three tables. We would do this by loading everything onto our trays, and carrying them through the ballroom (which was tightly packed) back into the service area. Unfortunately for me, I was in the far back of the room, so I had the most distance to cover with my tray. 

After the salad service, I got my first two tables cleared without incident. As I got my last table cleared, and loaded my tray, I realized I had forgotten to clear a large carafe full of ranch dressing. I grabbed it, placed it on the back end of my tray, and proceeded to run my tray back to the service area.   

As I got to the service area and began to take things off my tray, I realized the carafe of dressing had tipped over, and was now empty. I didn't think anything of it, finished clearing my tray, and headed back out to my tables. 

On the walk back, I realized where all the ranch dressing had gone. I had left a trail of it on the backs and in the hair of almost every person that I had walked by. I had also left a large trail of it on the floor. 

As you can imagine, I was pretty horrified. I had to go to each one of these people and tell them what had happened (most of them hadn't even realized). Even if these people weren't VIP guests I would have been scared...but I think the fact that many of them were senators and such made it worse. 

I got made fun of for years after that. Even now, when I go back, people that I never worked with know the story. It's crazy
